# Incident Reporting

Incidents are tracked in ServiceNow. An incident is the right channel
whenever something does not work as expected — a tool, a device, a virtual
session, or an access permission.

## When to Open an Incident

Open an incident when:

- A device or instrument behaves unexpectedly and the issue is not
  documented as known behavior.
- A virtual session disconnects repeatedly or fails to launch.
- An internal application returns errors or denies access despite an
  approved request.
- You suspect a piece of documentation is wrong and the impact is
  operational.

Do not open an incident for general questions, suggestions, or feedback.
Use the feedback channel for those, so that IT can analyze trends
separately from outages.

## What to Include

A useful incident contains four pieces of information: what you were
trying to do, what you observed, what you expected, and any error message
or screenshot that supports the description. Include the application name
exactly as it appears in the Application Catalog, because vague references
slow down triage.

## Submission

Submit the incident through the assistant or directly in ServiceNow. When
submitted through the assistant, the assistant collects the information
conversationally and creates the incident on your behalf using the
ServiceNow API. You will receive an incident reference number that you
can use to track progress.

## What Happens Next

Incident assignment, department routing, and follow-up communication are
handled outside the assistant — typically by email from the assigned
team. The assistant only creates the incident; it does not track its
later state.
